name: Sambisari Temple
significance: A ninth-century Shaiva temple compound that lay buried about five metres deep under Merapi volcanic deposits until a farmer struck its carved stone in 1966; excavation and reconstruction were completed in 1987, leaving the shrine sitting in a sunken courtyard.

name: Pura Luhur Batukaru
significance: One of Bali's Sad Kahyangan Jagad or six great directional sanctuaries, guarding the west and tied to the ancestors of the rajas of Tabanan; destroyed in 1604 and rebuilt in 1959, its principal shrine is a seven-tiered meru to Mahadewa on the slope of Bali's second-highest volcano.

name: Pura Dalem Sakenan
significance: A Balinese Hindu temple on Serangan island south of Denpasar, credited to the priest Mpu Kuturan and enlarged by villagers in 1982; the island was joined to the mainland by land reclamation and a bridge in 1996.

name: Kidal Temple
deity: Shiva, in the portrait form of the deified king Anusapati
significance: A slender East Javanese candi of about 1248 built as the mortuary shrine of the Singhasari king Anusapati, whose image is thought to have stood in its chamber as Shiva; its base carries three Javanese masks and reliefs of the Garuda story, and it was restored in the 1990s.

name: Sri Mariamman Temple, Medan
significance: Medan's oldest Hindu temple, raised in 1884 in the Kampung Madras quarter by Tamil labourers brought to the plantations of North Sumatra, and rededicated for Hindu Dharma worship in 1991; its gopuram makes it the focus of Thaipusam and Deepavali in the city.

name: Pura Kehen
deity: Hyang Api, the god of fire
significance: The royal temple of the Bangli kingdom, rising in terraces up a hillside with an eleven-tiered meru and a padmasana for Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva; copper-plate inscriptions from the 9th to 13th centuries mention it, and royal officials once swore their oaths of office here.
story: Villagers read the sacred banyan in the outer courtyard as an omen: a branch falling to the north-east foretells a king's death, one to the north-west a brahmin's.

name: Chau Say Tevoda
significance: A mid-12th-century Angkorian temple just east of Angkor Thom, begun under Suryavarman II with later work by Yasovarman II and Jayavarman VIII; it collapsed into some 4,000 scattered blocks and was rebuilt by a Chinese restoration team between 2000 and 2009.

name: Adichikkavu Sree Durga Devi Kshetram
significance: One of the older shrines of Pandanad village in central Travancore, dedicated to Vana Durga and managed by the Pandanad Karayogam; its sreekovil is built open at the top, the form prescribed for a forest Durga.

name: Halasuru Someshwara Temple
builtDisplay: 16th c. Vijayanagara work on a Chola-period shrine
significance: The oldest surviving temple in Bengaluru, traced to the Chola period and largely rebuilt under the late Vijayanagara Empire by the Yelahanka chief Kempe Gowda II; excavation at the site has uncovered a tank thought to be some 1,200 years old.
story: A local chief is said to have been told by Someshwara in a dream to build the temple with a hoard of buried treasure the god pointed him to.

name: Amirthakadeswarar Temple, Sakkottai
significance: A Shaiva temple near Kumbakonam sung in the 7th-century Tevaram and so counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams, built by the Cholas in the 9th century and expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks; it is linked to Sakya Nayanar, one of the sixty-three Saiva saints.
story: In the deluge the essence of creation is said to have come to rest here in a pot of nectar, which gave the place its old name Kalayanallur.

name: Gopinath Temple, Gopeshwar
significance: An old Shiva temple at Gopeshwar in Garhwal whose courtyard holds a five-metre trident of eight metals dated to the 12th century and inscribed in the name of Ashokchalla; broken images scattered around it suggest several more shrines once stood on the site.
story: The trident is said to be the one Shiva hurled at Kamadeva, which struck the ground here and stuck fast, and is believed to quiver at a true devotee's touch though no force can shift it.

name: Kadakkal Devi Temple
significance: A goddess shrine in eastern Kollam district unusual for having neither an idol nor a priest of the ordinary kind; the village around it was a centre of social-reform agitation in the decades before Indian independence.
story: The Devi is said to have come from Tamil Nadu with four sisters and to have killed a trader named Panayappan who had cheated her family, then settled into his wooden shop, which became the sanctum.

name: Kalarickal Manikanda Swami Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Thrikkodithanam in Kottayam district that also holds the tomb of Kalarickal Gurunathan, remembered as a master of kalari payattu who served the local ruler.

name: Gorakhnath Math
significance: The head monastery of the Nath sampradaya, spread over some 52 acres at Gorakhpur on the spot where Gorakshanath is held to have practised; the city takes its name from the saint, and the math has long been a centre of the order's religious and public life.
story: A lamp called the Divya Jyoti is said to have burned in the math without interruption since Gorakshanath's own time.

name: Jatashankar
significance: A natural cave shrine north of Pachmarhi in the Satpura hills where stalagmites are venerated as self-formed lingams, fed by two springs whose pools run notably cold and warm.
story: The cave is said to be where Shiva hid himself from the fury of the demon Bhasmasura; the name joins jata, matted hair, with Shankara.

name: Alappancode Easwara Kala Bhoothathan Temple
deity: Easwara Kala Bhoothathan, a form of Shiva, worshipped with Ayyappan and Bhadrakali
significance: A pilgrimage centre in the Malayalam-speaking belt of Kanyakumari district, run by a hereditary trust, where Easwara Kala Bhoothathan is worshipped alongside Ayyappan and Bhadrakali.

name: Alattiyur Hanuman Temple
significance: A temple near Tirur whose presiding deity is Rama but which is known throughout Kerala for its Hanuman shrine; held in trust successively by the Alathiyur Nambudiris, the rulers of Vettathunad and the Zamorin of Kozhikode, it is now the leading temple of the Malabar Devaswom Board.
story: The image shows Rama giving Hanuman his instructions before the search for Sita in Lanka, with Hanuman leaning in to listen and Lakshmana standing apart so as not to overhear.

name: Iringole Kavu
deity: Durga, worshipped as Saraswati at dawn, Vana Durga at noon and Bhadrakali at night
significance: A goddess temple set inside a surviving sacred grove near Perumbavoor, counted among the 108 Durga temples traditionally ascribed to Parasurama; long held by local families, it now comes under the Travancore Devaswom Board.
story: The infant girl Kamsa seized in place of Krishna, an incarnation of Yoga-Nidra, is said to have slipped from his grasp into the air and settled in this forest as the goddess of the grove.

name: Jagdish Temple, Udaipur
significance: The largest temple in Udaipur, completed in 1651 by Maharana Jagat Singh I beside the city palace and in continuous worship ever since; a flight of thirty-two marble steps past a brass Garuda leads to the black-stone image of Jagannath under a 79-foot spire.

name: Kalamassery Mahaganapathy Temple
significance: A modern Ganesha temple founded in 1981 by N. Reghunatha Menon and rebuilt in traditional Kerala form in 2000, now run by a family trust; it is known for its Ashta Dravya Maha Ganapathy Havana and the Aanayoottu elephant feeding held at the start of Karkkidakam.

name: Javari Temple, Khajuraho
deity: Vishnu, whose broken image stands in the sanctum; the temple is also described as dedicated to Shiva
significance: A small, finely proportioned Chandela temple in the eastern group at Khajuraho, part of the UNESCO World Heritage site; it is entered through an elaborate makara torana arch, and its principal image survives only as a headless torso.

name: Irumkulangara Durga Devi Temple
significance: An old Devi temple less than two kilometres from the Padmanabhaswamy temple in Thiruvananthapuram, sharing its thanthri and historically linked to it by priests who came across the backwater by country boat; it was rebuilt in Kerala vastu form and reconsecrated in December 2009.

name: Agroha Dham
deity: Mahalakshmi, with shrines to Saraswati and Maharaja Agrasena
significance: A modern pilgrimage complex at Agroha, the town the Agrawal community holds to be its place of origin, built between 1976 and 1984 by the Agroha Vikas Trust after a national Aggarwal convention resolved on it; the historic settlement declined after its capture in 1194.

name: Jarai-ka-Math
significance: A red sandstone panchayatana temple at Barua Sagar near Jhansi, ascribed to the Gurjara-Pratihara emperor Mihira Bhoja around 860 and protected by the Archaeological Survey of India since 1928; its main image is lost, leaving only the pedestal and a jewelled stone foot, and its walls carry sculpture often compared with Khajuraho.

name: Kalikambal Temple
significance: A temple on Thambu Chetty Street in old George Town, moved to its present site on 1 March 1640 when the English East India Company built Fort St George over its original seashore location, with construction continuing to 1678; Shivaji is recorded as having worshipped here on 3 October 1677, and its rajagopuram was added between 1976 and 1983.
story: The goddess is said to have been worshipped here first in a fierce form, which Adi Shankara replaced with the serene Kamakshi.

name: Kalikamba Temple
significance: A temple on Lower Car Street in Mangalore closely associated with the Vishwakarma Brahmana community of smiths and carpenters; its sanctums were rebuilt in granite in 2000, and it holds a ten-day Ugadi festival and a mass upanayana every five years.

name: Kalika Siva Temple
deity: Shiva, as a lingam in a circular yonipitha
significance: A small medieval sandstone shrine of about four metres beside the Manikarnika tank embankment just outside the Kapilesvara temple compound in Bhubaneswar; still in worship, it was repaired by Odisha State Archaeology and is looked after by the Kapilesvara Trust Board.

name: Gosagaresvar Siva Temple
deity: Gosagaresvar Siva, a lingam in a circular yonipitha
significance: A fourteenth-century sandstone Shiva temple in Bhubaneswar built in dry ashlar masonry, with three Shiva shrines inside its enclosure; still a living temple, it was repaired by Odisha State Archaeology under the Tenth and Eleventh Finance Commission awards.

name: Hanuman Tok
significance: A hilltop Hanuman shrine about 11 km above Gangtok at some 2,195 m, raised over a sacred stone by the administrator Appaji Pant in 1950 and completed in 1952; the Indian Army later took over the surrounding land and maintains it, and it commands a wide view of the Kangchenjunga range.
story: Hanuman is said to have set down to rest at this spot while carrying the Sanjeevani herb from Dunagiri to revive Lakshmana.

name: Kadeshwari Devi Temple
deity: Kadeshwari, the mother goddess as Shakti
significance: A goddess temple on the headland behind Bandra Fort at Land's End in Mumbai; the municipal corporation moved in 2006 to build a protective bund after the sea began eating away its foundations and boundary walls.

name: Kalabhairavi Temple
deity: Chamunda, four-armed and seated on a corpse
significance: A twelfth-century shrine inside the Jaleswar Siva temple precinct at Kalarahanga in Bhubaneswar, attributed to King Madhusudhan Deva and guarded by Shaiva dvarapalas; still in worship, it was repaired by the state archaeology department.

name: Jyotir Math
deity: Narayana, with the goddess as Purnagiri
significance: The northern of the four cardinal pithams traditionally established by Adi Shankara, seat of the Shankaracharya of the north at Joshimath in Garhwal; it stood vacant for some 165 years until Brahmananda Saraswati was installed on 11 May 1941 and built the present thirty-room monastery and the Purnagiri Devi shrine.

name: Harihara Deula
deity: Shiva and Vishnu, as the twin Siddhesvara and Nilamadhava shrines
significance: A pair of twin temples at Gandharadi on the Mahanadi in Boudh district, built by the Somavamshi kings in the late tenth century, one holding a shivalinga and the other a four-armed chlorite Vishnu; the pairing is read as a statement of Shaiva-Vaishnava accord and marks a formative stage of Kalinga architecture.

name: Kadampanad Bhagavathy Temple
significance: A Bhagavathy temple at Kadampanad about 12 km from Adoor, managed by karayogam unit 232 of the Nair Service Society; its ten-day festival in Meenam ends with an aaraattu procession accompanied by caparisoned elephants.

name: Kadri Manjunath Temple
builtDisplay: 10th-11th c. origin; rebuilt in stone 14th c.
significance: A major Mangalore temple that grew out of the Buddhist Kadarika Vihara, keeping a metre-and-a-half bronze Lokeshwara installed by the Alupa king Kundavarma and dated by inscription to 968; the shrine was rebuilt entirely in stone in the 14th century and carries inscriptions in Tulu, Kannada and Malayalam.
story: Parashurama is said to have done penance at Kadali Kshetra, where Shiva appeared to him as Manjunatha with Parvati.

name: Ajaikapada Bhairava Temple
deity: Ekapada Bhairava, an aspect of Shiva, with a shivalinga in the sanctum
builtDisplay: early 10th c. origin; rebuilt early 20th c.
significance: A shrine near the Alaka branch of the Mahanadi in Jagatsinghpur district traced by archaeological survey to the early 10th century under the Somavamsi kings; ruined by flooding and invasion, it was rebuilt in the early twentieth century around its one-footed Bhairava image.

name: Amaramkavu
significance: A forest-goddess shrine set in what the article calls the largest surviving sacred grove in Idukki district, about three acres of protected biodiversity on the edge of Thodupuzha town.

name: Jaleswar Siva Temple Precinct
deity: Shiva, as a lingam in a circular yonipitha
significance: A walled twelfth-century Shiva precinct at Kalarahanga on the northern edge of Bhubaneswar, once ringed by water on all four sides, whose sanctum lingam sits 1.15 m below the chandrasila; it was repaired by Odisha State Archaeology.
story: A king of Chudangagada devoted to Lingaraja is said to have been told in a dream to raise a temple at the lotus pond where the lord dwelt as Jalasayi, and built it on the pond's western embankment.

name: Indralath Temple
significance: The tallest brick temple in Odisha, standing at Ranipur-Jharial in Balangir district and dated by the Archaeological Survey of India, which maintains it, to the 10th-11th century; its images of Narasimha, Vishnu, Ganesha and Kartikeya point to a site where Shaiva and Vaishnava worship met.
story: The temple takes its name from the belief that Indra himself first worshipped Shiva at this spot and raised a shrine over it.

name: ISKCON Temple, Chennai
deity: Radha and Krishna, with Jagannath, Baladeva and Subhadra
significance: A Gaudiya Vaishnava temple on Hare Krishna Land off the East Coast Road, begun in March 2002 and consecrated on 26 April 2012 at a cost of about 100 million rupees on 45,000 square feet, funded by some 8,000 life patrons; it descends from the Chennai centre ISKCON opened at Kilpauk in 1975.
